candidate.answerReason: Checking all possible denominators gives the unique assignment W=3, X=1, Y=4, Z=2, so W+Y=7.

methods.label: Restrict the denominator and check cases
methods.explanation:
All four numbers are positive, so \(Y/Z>0\). The equation therefore requires \(W/X>1\), which means \(W>X\). Consequently, \(X\) can only be \(1,2,\) or \(3\). Check these cases while keeping all four numbers different.

If \(X=1\), then \(Y/Z=W-1\) must be a whole number. The only whole-number ratio of two different numbers among \(2,3,4\) is \(4/2=2\). This gives \(Y=4\), \(Z=2\), and \(W=3\).

If \(X=2\), then \(W=3\) or \(4\). For \(W=3\), the required ratio is \(Y/Z=1/2\), but the unused numbers \(1,4\) give only \(1/4\) or \(4\). For \(W=4\), the required ratio is \(1\), which is impossible because \(Y\ne Z\).

If \(X=3\), then \(W=4\), requiring \(Y/Z=1/3\). The unused numbers \(1,2\) give only \(1/2\) or \(2\), so this case is impossible.

These cases exhaust the possibilities. The surviving assignment satisfies
\[
\frac31-\frac42=3-2=1.
\]
Thus \(W+Y=3+4=7\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
